title: Series-Parallel Hybrid SOT-MRAM Computing-in-Memory Macro with Multi-Method Modulation for High Area and Energy Efficiency
problem: Existing MRAM-series and MRAM-parallel architectures for computing-in-memory suffer from high energy costs and low flexibility, respectively, limiting their applicability for neural network inference.
motivation: Computing-in-memory demonstrates superiority for neural network inference; exploring SOT-MRAM-based CIM implementations can provide better area and energy efficiency.
method: The paper proposes a series-parallel hybrid SOT-MRAM CIM macro with a 6T-4J weight group architecture. The design combines serial and parallel MTJ configurations to balance energy efficiency and architectural flexibility. A multi-method modulation scheme operates from input unit to array level, supporting configurable precision (2/4/6/8-bit). The macro was designed and verified in both 180nm and 28nm technology nodes.
key_novelty: Series-parallel hybrid MTJ configuration that combines serial and parallel modes to simultaneously achieve energy efficiency and flexibility compared to pure serial or parallel architectures.
contributions: Series-parallel hybrid architecture for SOT-MRAM CIM addressing energy-flexibility trade-offs
Multi-method modulation scheme with configurable 2-8 bit input precision
Implementation and verification in 180nm and 28nm technology nodes
Achieved energy efficiency of 23.7-29.6 Tops/W at 8-bit precision
primary_theme: SOT-MRAM CIM macro with hybrid MTJ architecture
